depiction.primary_object: six-petaled flower blossom above two curved leaves
modifiers: diagonal slash from top-left to bottom-right
depiction.composition: single object, front view, crossed out by diagonal bar

readings.meaning: weeds, dead plants, or unwanted garden growth to remove
pollen allergy or hay fever protection
cancel or skip flower delivery / no-flowers policy

ambiguity: Originally a camera UI glyph for 'macro mode off', which most people outside photography settings read as 'weeding', 'remove dead plants', or 'allergy / no pollen'.

reasoning: A flower crossed out by a diagonal slash literally denotes 'no flowers' (or 'macro mode off' in camera interfaces). In a to-do list it fits tasks about weeding, deadheading or removing dead/toxic plants, pollen allergies, and cancelling flower deliveries; it must be distinguished from the unslashed flower used for planting or buying blooms.
